instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Orders from the Shadows
cards.instruction: Hide that you set the problem in motion while quietly directing how everyone responds.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The crates went to Leeds. I used your sample email; tell the manager we're correcting the address.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That was a training example. Your email sent them there. Shall I forward it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, the sample. Forward only the corrected address. She needs to know where they're going now.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She wants a timeline before she'll pay for another van.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start with when we discovered the error. I'll arrange the van while you write.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I ticked all the wedding bookings like you did. Now the couples have cancellation emails; please call them while I sort the screen.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I ticked them to export the list. You pressed cancel. The log has your initials.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, the selected list. Keep that log here; give the couples replacement dates while I check it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Bulk restore sends an email naming whoever cancelled. I could put the dates back manually, but that takes all afternoon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll put them back manually. I'll stay and read every date out; you won't have to do the afternoon alone.

cards.title: Not Up for Debate
cards.instruction: Keep the conversation from examining where your authority comes from or whether it is legitimate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my name in the top box like yours. List me as cafe shift leader, then we'll order the milk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's the emergency-contact box. Who appointed you shift leader? I normally do the order.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, first contact. You're good at ordering; how much milk for tomorrow?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll order it, but I'll write 'leadership unconfirmed' beside your name.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use a fresh sheet for the order. Just list the milk and quantities; the supplier doesn't need our names.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Costume inspection. Unlock the cupboard, please; I've pinned on a badge like yours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wore mine to play a policeman. Who sent you? The cupboard's locked because of moths.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, costume badges. Let's look at the moth damage before it spreads.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll get the wardrobe manager. She'll ask who authorized your inspection.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell her I'm here to help with the moths. Show her the damage first; we can do introductions afterwards.

cards.title: For Stability’s Sake
cards.instruction: Hide a destabilizing truth because you believe the current balance of power must be protected.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put the director's confident 'business as usual' on the launch programme. Keep her name above the department heads.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That was her automatic email reply. She's resigned; the notice is in the printer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, a continuity message. Put the notice in my drawer; the heads will each claim the launch if they see it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're already asking who gets her opening speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll read it on her behalf. Give each head the same short introduction; none of them takes her slot.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've called the fair arch 'donated,' just as the chair did. Leave that word in the briefing; everyone needs confidence in her today.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She paid for it with the stall money. Calling it donated doesn't leave us any cash.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, it's the cash we need to settle. Keep the spending out of the briefing; they'll replace her before we open.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll cover it, but she has to sign an IOU.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Have her sign in the office after the welcome. Let her open the fair before anyone sees her borrowing the money.

cards.title: Name Your Backers
cards.instruction: Get someone to reveal who supports their position, who authorized it, and who benefits from it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've ticked the workshop-closure sheet like you. That's two approvals. Before I send it, who backed the decision?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My tick means received. The director approved the closure; please just send the notice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, two acknowledgements. Who supported the director when she proposed it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sales. They're getting the floor space, but leave them out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then name who approved that transfer. If Sales gets our workshop, I want their support on the notice too.

beats.text: I've circled the cheap roof tile like you did. We're both recommending it, then. Who else backed this choice?

beats.speaker: A

cards.title: Strategic Retreat
cards.instruction: Describe every loss of control as a deliberate concession made from strength.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've taken off my club badge like you. A gracious handover; I want you to have room to grow as chair.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I took mine off to put on the chair's badge. You lost the vote. I need the cupboard key for tonight's match.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, clearing the old equipment. I'm releasing the key so you can practise responsibility.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Remove yourself as administrator too. I can't change the fixtures while you have the override.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Gladly. I'll give up the override as well. You should learn to make decisions without my safety net.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've rolled up the exhibition posters like you. We're giving the gallery space to pursue its smaller ambitions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm taking them down because they rejected your show. Shall I collect the paintings too?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, clearing the display. Yes, withdraw the paintings; let them see how the room works without my best pieces.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're already outside. I'll bring the van before it rains.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. We'll free up the pavement as well. They can have an unobstructed entrance when you've loaded the van.
